correctness.rationale: Length six is the length of the intrinsic defect I_P/J_P, not the colength of a chosen embedded primary ideal. Independently set z=x_5 and y_i=x_i-z. On the hyperplane, y_5=0 and y_4=-sum_{i=0}^3 y_i; S_2=Q=sum_{i=0}^4 y_i^2, by characteristic three. The Jacobian differences are Qy_i-y_i^3; the fifth is redundant. This makes the projective ideal the extension of a homogeneous four-variable ideal with z free. If Q=0, all y_i vanish; otherwise rescale to Q=1. The five y_i then lie in {0,1,-1}, have sum zero, and exactly four are nonzero (one nonzero entry cannot give sum zero). They have two entries of each sign and one zero. Up to sign these are exactly the fifteen directions of the pair-partition lines. An independent exact graded-lex calculation gives numerator 1-4t^3+11t^6-9t^7+t^9 over (1-t)^4 for the four-variable quotient, and direct evaluation at the fifteen directions gives ranks 1,4,10,15 in degrees 0 through 3 (surjectivity persists by multiplying by a linear form nonvanishing on the directions over the algebraic closure). The difference in four variables is t^3+4t^4+t^5, hence a graded finite-length defect supported at the origin; adjoining z and projectivizing makes it a length-six defect at the vertex only. The independent calculation uses the transformed ideal and an evaluation set defined by Q=1; the uploaded checker was read but not executed.
